newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh seeks over $4.0 bln investment in power.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh seeks over $4.0 bln investment in power.

text.p: Bangladesh on Monday told international donors it would require 185 billion taka ($4.2 billion) of investment over the next five years to boost its power generating capacity.

"A country like Bangladesh can ill afford this colossal amount by itself. We need foreign capital to meet our requirements for power," a government official quoted Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan as saying at a donors' conference in Dhaka.

Major financiers to Bangladesh's energy sector -- Japan, Britain, Germany, Norway, Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the World Bank -- began a four-day meeting in the Bangladesh capital on Monday to frame a future lending strategy.
Energy ministry officials said they would seek fresh funding support for 40 on-going and new projects in the power and gas sectors.
Donor sources said they now preferred channelling funds through private sources than through the government.
Khan said Bangladesh needed to raise its electricity generation to 3,100 megawatts by the year 2,000 and 4,600 megawatts by 2005 from current levels of 1,850 megawatts.
A prolonged freeze on foreign assistance has crippled Bangladesh's power sector.

Energy Ministry officials said theft in public power distribution system and the government's reluctance in opening electricity generation to the private sector led to the freeze about four years ago.
"We are fast liberalising our policies, removing bottlenecks to allow foreign private capital into our investment-hungry energy sector," the Energy Minister said.

Energy ministry officials said the cabinet would approve agreements on power purchases from private generators and security packages for them in one week, removing the last major hurdles to private power generation.
Khan drew donors' attention to the coal sector and said the government was planning to develop two more prospective mines with reserves of about 1,450 million tonnes.
Development of a 300 million-tonne mine at northern Dinajpur district had already begun.
Bangladesh, with proven natural gas reserves of more than 10 trillion cubic feet, has signed gas exploration deals with half a dozen international firms.
More than a dozen exploration firms are vying for stakes in 15 remaining prospective blocks currently on offer.
